title: Daily pill shrinks tumors in pancreatic cancer trial, offering new hope
paragraphs: A daily pill called daraxonrasib has shown promise in shrinking or eliminating tumors in some pancreatic cancer patients, marking what experts call the biggest advance in decades for one of the deadliest cancers.

In early clinical trials, tumors disappeared in one of 12 patients receiving the drug with chemotherapy, and nearly all 61 participants with advanced pancreatic cancer saw their tumors stop growing. However, doctors caution it is unclear how long the drug controls the disease and it is not a cure.

Cancer Research UK called the findings "incredibly exciting," noting the drug targets RAS mutations found in most pancreatic cancers. The treatment could also help patients with other cancers, though longer studies are needed to confirm remission durability.

title: Islam Projected to Surpass Christianity as World's Largest Religion by 2035
paragraphs: Islam is projected to become the world's largest religion by 2035, surpassing Christianity in number of adherents, according to demographic projections released Wednesday by the Pew Research Center.

The Washington-based research center forecasts that Christians will fall behind Muslims within a decade, a historic shift given Christians were nearly three times more numerous at the start of the 20th century. By 2070, Islam is expected to represent nearly 36% of the global population, compared to 29% for Christianity.

The growth is driven by demographic factors, including young populations and high fertility rates in regions like sub-Saharan Africa, while the Asia-Pacific region is projected to host half of the world's Muslims within 50 years. The projections measure declared religious affiliation, not actual practice, and the share of religiously unaffiliated people is expected to decline globally despite rising secularism in Western countries.

title: Trump Summit Marks Win for China and Russia
paragraphs: The trilateral summit between US President Trump, Russian President Putin, and Chinese President Xi in Shenzhen is seen as a symbolic victory for China and Russia, signaling the end of US global hegemony. Trump's participation is interpreted as recognizing the leaders as equals.

The summit produced a joint statement, not yet confirmed by the White House, asserting that immunity for state officials is fundamental, a clause tailored to protect Putin from an ICC arrest warrant. The leaders also agreed to continue dialogue on reducing nuclear risk, but made no binding commitments.

The meeting underscores a shift to a multipolar world with the US and China as major poles, plus Russia. Polls show China is viewed more favorably than the US in most countries, and the summit provides Xi with a strong political platform.

title: IEA: Iran war permanently reshapes global energy priorities
paragraphs: The International Energy Agency reports that the Iran war will permanently reshape global energy priorities, with lasting impacts on security and affordability. The conflict has fundamentally altered how nations approach their energy systems.

Energy-hungry nations will prioritize secure electricity supplies, benefiting renewables like solar and nuclear power, while keeping coal as a crisis backup. The IEA projects oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz could drop from 20 million barrels daily before the war to under 2 million by 2035.

The report coincides with COP31 climate talks in Turkey, where electrification is a key focus. IEA officials note a unique convergence between energy security policies and climate transition goals, though coal may retain momentum as a fallback option for some economies.

title: Malaria vaccine shows 87% efficacy in phase 1 trial
paragraphs: A novel malaria vaccine, PfSPZ-LARC2, demonstrated 87% efficacy in a phase 1 trial, preventing infection in most vaccinated participants exposed to the parasite.

In the trial, only two of 15 vaccinated individuals developed malaria after a controlled challenge, while all seven placebo recipients became infected. The live-attenuated vaccine uses genetic deletions to halt parasite growth in the liver, prompting a broad immune response.

The findings were presented at the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene meeting. Researchers highlighted the vaccine's durable, cross-strain protection, a key factor given malaria's geographic diversity and the over 600,000 annual deaths worldwide.

title: Anthropic tops $3 trillion in Nasdaq debut, beating SpaceX's June listing
paragraphs: Anthropic soared past $3 trillion in market value during its Nasdaq debut, surpassing SpaceX's June listing as investors rushed to buy shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company. The stock opened at $US111.5, 34 per cent above its IPO price of $US83.

The stellar debut caps a turbulent week for the AI sector, marked by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit and shifting Wall Street attention to rival OpenAI. Anthropic sold 980 million shares, with proceeds potentially reaching $US93.5 billion if underwriters exercise their option, plus $US26 billion from a private placement involving major tech firms.

Based on the IPO price, CEO Dario Amodei and six co-founders, owning about 10 per cent combined, had stakes valued near $US150 billion. The listing is expected to create thousands of paper millionaires, while analysts see Anthropic as a benchmark for the AI trade amid debate over whether the boom is a bubble.
